Latin word

anima

anima, animae f.

noun, first declension

the breath, the air breathed in and out; the soul

In this lexicon

  • breath

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 324; Ter. Ph. 868: animam compressī, I held my breath (Lewis & Short)

  • soul

    the recommended word · classical · Sall. J. 2.2: ingeniī facinora, sīcut anima, immortālia sunt (Lewis & Short); Vulg. Lc. 1.46

  • Dum anima est, spēs est.: where there’s life there’s hope

    modern

Examples

  • Magnificat anima mea Dominum

    My soul magnifies the LordVulg. Lc. 1.46

    In the entry for soul

  • Benedīc, anima mea, Dominō

    Bless the Lord, my soulVulg. Ps. 102 (103), 2

    In the entry for soul

  • angusta est domus animae meae quō veniās ad eam: dīlātētur abs tē. ruīnōsa est: refice eam

    the house of my soul is too small for you to come into: let it be enlarged by you. It is falling down: rebuild itAug. Conf. 1.5.6

    In the entry for soul
